As per office report, notice has been served on respondent no. 2 yet no one appeared on his/her behalf.
Heard learned counsel for appellant, learned A.G.A. for the State-Respondent and perused the paper book.

This Criminal Appeal under Section 14-A(2) Scheduled Castes & Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act has been filed questioning the correctness of the order dated 25.8.2022 passed by Special Judge (SC/ST Act)/ Additional District and Sessions Judge, Lalitpur arising out of Case Crime no. 411 of 2022, under Sections 376, 354, 504, 506 IPC and Section 3(2)(v) of SC/ST Act, P.S.
Kotwali Lalitpur, District Lalitpur, whereby his prayer for bail has been rejected.
According to prosecution version, informant/ prosecutrix lodged FIR on 8.7.2022 at around 20:17 hours stating therein that on 7.7.2022 at around 11:00 am she was coming with her husband to village Virdha for marketing; the accused met them and had given lift to them on his motorcycle on pretext that he will leave them at village Virdha; she came with her husband at village Virdha from Brijendra Singh Thakur vs State Of U.P. And Another on 22 March, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/150013270/

sentences.text: where she had gone to place of her relative and accused took her husband with him towards market and got him administered liquor, after sometime he came to her and stated that her husband was calling her and on that pretext he took her at an isolated place where he committed rape on her and threatened her and also abused her by caste specific word.

It is contended by counsel for the appellant that there are material contradiction in the FIR version as well as statement recorded under Section 161 and 164 Cr.P.C. and same has been pointed out by the C.O. during investigation;
her medical examination was conducted on 9.7.2022 wherein doctor has written that no sign of use of force is found on her person; final opinion can be given after getting FSL report, however in FSL report, no sign of sperm or semen was found on under garments, no blood was found there; victim in her statement under Section 164 Cr.P.C. has stated that after the incident, accused left her by his motorcycle near a well, she informed her son about the incident thereafter this report was lodged on next day.

He next submitted that there is contradiction in the statement of the victim made to the doctor, who conducted her medical examination and her version before the police and Magistrate;
in FIR as well as in statement under section 161 and 164 Cr.P.C. victim has stated that accused had given lift to her and her husband, however doctor had recorded her statement at the time of her medical examination that accused had got lift in motorcycle by which victim and her husband was traveling and all three came to market by that motorcycle; no independent witness has been enjoined in support of the prosecution version; accused has not been assigned any prior criminal history; he is in jail since 23.7.2022; learned trial court has rejected the bail application of the appellant without examining the material on record.
Per contra, learned AGA has vehemently opposed the prayer for bail and supported the impugned order.

He submitted that FIR version has been supported by the victim in her statement under Section 161 and 164 Cr.P.C. and by the statement of her husband whom she narrated incident just after uniting with him after incident; he also pointed out that doctor who conducted her medical examination has recorded small abrasion on wrist .5 cm lateral side of left wrist.
However he could not point out anything material on the contrary.

Considering the facts and circumstances of the case, victim is married lady, in FSL report, nothing incriminating is found against the appellant and period of incarceration and keeping in view the fact that the trial of the case is not likely to be concluded in near future, the appeal has substance and it is, accordingly, allowed.
Impugned order dated 25.8.2022 is, hereby, set aside.

Let appellant, Brijendra Singh Thakur, be released on bail in aforesaid Case Crime on his furnishing a personal bond and two reliable sureties of the like amount to the satisfaction of the court concerned with the following conditions:
(i) The appellant shall file an undertaking to the effect that he shall not seek any adjournment on the dates fixed for evidence, if the witnesses are present in Court.

In case of default of this condition, it shall be open for the trial court to treat it as abuse of liberty of bail and pass orders in accordance with law;
(ii) The appellant shall remain present before the trial court on each date fixed, either personally or through his counsel.
